seo.og_description: Silver, leather, melhfa and the rhythm of daily Saharan commerce in the heart of Laâyoune.

name: Souk Soune
hero_subtitle: The traditional bazaar of Laâyoune – Sahrawi silver, camel leather, colourful melhfa fabrics, and the authentic pulse of local life.

overview.title: The Everyday Heart of Sahrawi Commerce
overview.p1: Souk Soune is the main traditional market area of Laâyoune where locals come to buy and sell everyday goods, crafts and regional specialities. Unlike the polished medinas of Marrakech or Fes, this is a working Saharan market with a strong local character.
overview.p2: You will find stalls and small shops offering Sahrawi silver jewellery with geometric designs, leather goods made from camel hide, the distinctive colourful melhfa (the traditional women’s wrap), textiles, spices, and practical household items.
overview.p3: It is one of the best places in the city to observe authentic daily life, practise a little bargaining, and bring home meaningful souvenirs that reflect the culture of the southern provinces.

moods.title: When to Visit Souk Soune
moods.subtitle: Morning is by far the best time for atmosphere and choice.

1.title: Busiest & Most Authentic
1.desc: From opening until early afternoon the market is lively with local shoppers. This is the best window for photos, people-watching and finding the widest selection.

2.title: Quieter Pace
2.desc: Activity slows after lunch. Some stalls may close or reduce their displays. Still pleasant for a shorter visit if mornings are not possible.

3.title: Extra Energy
3.desc: Certain days (especially around weekends or special markets) bring more traders and a bigger selection of livestock or seasonal goods.

food.title: Snacks & Drinks Around the Souk
food.p1: The market itself is more about shopping than fine dining, but you will find simple local food options nearby.
food.li1: Street grills and small stands offering brochettes, kofta and fresh bread.
food.li2: Juice stalls with orange, avocado or mixed fruit juices.
food.li3: Traditional mint tea or Sahrawi Atay in nearby cafés.
food.li4: Pastries and simple sweets from local bakeries.
food.li5: For a fuller meal, the restaurants around Place Mechouar or Avenue Makkah are only a short walk away.
food.p2: Eating in or near the souk is casual, inexpensive and very local.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Souk Soune

1.title: Bargaining & Etiquette
1.desc: Polite bargaining is expected for crafts and non-fixed-price items. Smile, take your time, and never feel pressured. Asking permission before photographing people is always appreciated.

2.title: What to Buy
2.desc: Look for genuine Sahrawi silver jewellery, camel-leather items, and the colourful melhfa. These make the most meaningful and authentic souvenirs from Laâyoune.

3.title: Getting There & Safety
3.desc: The market is in central Laâyoune and easily reached on foot or by petit taxi from Place Mechouar. It is a normal local market – busy but generally safe. Keep valuables secure as in any crowded place.

q1.question: Is Souk Soune free to enter?
q1.answer: Yes, it is a public traditional market open to everyone at no charge.

q2.question: What are the best things to buy?
q2.answer: Sahrawi silver jewellery, camel-leather goods, and the colourful melhfa fabrics are the most characteristic and authentic purchases.

q3.question: Do I need to bargain?
q3.answer: For crafts and many non-fixed items, polite bargaining is normal and expected. Fixed-price shops also exist.

q4.question: Is the market safe for tourists?
q4.answer: Yes. It is a busy local market. Use normal big-city precautions (secure bags, be aware of your surroundings) and you will be fine.

q5.question: How long should I spend there?
q5.answer: 1 to 2 hours is usually enough to explore, take photos, and make a few purchases at a relaxed pace.
